<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>mysql-jdbc-demo</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>mysql-jdbc-demo</name>
    <description>Maven Java project demonstrating MySQL connectivity via JDBC</description>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <mysql.connector.version>8.4.0</mysql.connector.version>
        <slf4j.version>2.0.13</slf4j.version>
        <junit.version>5.10.2</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>com.mysql</groupId>
            <artifactId>mysql-connector-j</artifactId>
            <version>${mysql.connector.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
            <artifactId>slf4j-simple</artifactId>
            <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>com.mysql</groupId>
            <artifactId>mysql-connector-j</artifactId>
            <version>${mysql.connector.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
            <type>test-jar</type>
            <classifier>tests</classifier>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <finalName>${project.artifactId}</finalName>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.13.0</version>
            </plugin>

            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.2.5</version>
            </plugin>

            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.3</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <phase>package</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>shade</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <createDependencyReducedPom>false</createDependencyReducedPom>
                            <transformers>
                                <transformer
                                        implementation="org.apache.maven.plugins.shade.resource.ManifestResourceTransformer">
                                    <mainClass>com.example.jdbc.Main</mainClass>
                                </transformer>
                            </transformers>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

Now a test. Testing JDBC without a DB is tricky. I can use H2 in MySQL mode for a test, or use Testcontainers. To keep it simple and verifiable offline, add H2 test dependency and test the repository against H2 in MySQL compatibility mode. But the schema.sql uses MySQL-specific syntax. Let me create a test schema.

Actually, let me add H2 test dependency and a test that exercises UserRepository. That gives real value and can run offline (H2 is a small dep downloaded by Maven). But network to Maven central—need to verify build. Let me add H2 and a test.

Let me update pom to remove that weird test-jar dependency I added (mysql-connector-j tests classifier) — that's unnecessary and may not exist. Remove it. Add H2.

Now the test. Use H2 in-memory with MySQL mode. The `Database` class hardcodes `com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver` load in static initializer, which means tests can't use H2 because loading the MySQL driver is fine (it's on test classpath), but `DriverManager.getConnection` with H2 URL works as long as H2 driver registers itself. The static initializer only forces MySQL driver load; it doesn't prevent H2. H2 auto-registers via service loader. So fine.

But `Database` doesn't let me inject a URL—it takes DbConfig. DbConfig is constructed only via load(). I could add a constructor/factory for tests. Let me add a static factory `DbConfig.of(url, user, password)`.

part.text:
Done. Maven project scaffolded and `mvn clean verify` passes (2 tests).

Structure:
- `pom.xml` — `com.mysql:mysql-connector-j` 8.4.0, Java 21, shade plugin builds a runnable fat jar (`com.example.jdbc.Main`)
- `src/main/java/com/example/jdbc/` — `DbConfig` (loads `db.properties`, env overrides `DB_URL`/`DB_USER`/`DB_PASSWORD`), `Database` (driver + connections), `UserRepository` (parameterized CRUD), `User`, `Main`
- `src/main/resources/db.properties` — connection settings; `schema.sql` — sample table
- `src/test/java/.../UserRepositoryTest.java` — runs against in-memory H2 (MySQL mode), no server needed

Run it with `mvn package` then `java -jar target/mysql-jdbc-demo.jar`. Set credentials via env vars rather than committing them.
